citation: Ludwig, M., & Song, M. (2015). Evaluation of professional development in the use of arts-integrated activities with mathematics content: Findings from the evaluation of the Wolf Trap Arts in Education Model Development and Dissemination Grant. Final grant report. Washington, DC: American Institutes for Research. (ERIC No. ED553403)
report_number: AIR Wolf Trap AEMDD Final Grant Report (January 2015); ERIC ED553403
design: School-level cluster RCT; 22 elementary schools in one large suburban district randomized to Wolf Trap arts-integrated-mathematics PD (treatment) vs business-as-usual (control); analytic sample 18 schools (10 treatment, 8 control); prekindergarten (incl. Head Start) and kindergarten; subject = mathematics. Two staggered cohorts (Group 1 = 6 schools recruited 2011, Group 2 = 16 schools recruited 2012) pooled in impact analyses.
problems: The report gives only group means, the mean difference, a p-value, and an effect size (defined in footnote 10 as raw mean difference divided by pooled within-group SD, i.e. a student-level Cohen's d) for each year. It does NOT report the HLM impact coefficient (gamma01), its standard error, group SDs, the exact treatment/control split of the analysis samples, or any ICC. Significance (p<.01) comes from a 2-level HLM (students within schools) that adjusts for baseline EMDA and covariates and accounts for clustering, but the reported effect-size MAGNITUDE is the unadjusted student-level d, so it is NOT pretest-adjusted and NOT cluster-adjusted. Therefore g was computed by applying Hedges' J to the reported d, and g_var/g_se were computed from the n-based variance formula; n_t/n_c are estimates derived by splitting the reported analysis N (369 Year1, 334 Year2) in proportion to the assessed-sample T/C ratios (220/174 Year1, 198/156 Year2) because exact analysis-sample splits are not given. n_clusters=18; ICC not reported (not guessed). The g values therefore need central cluster correction (Hedges 2007) once an ICC is supplied. Outcome subject is mathematics -> STEM. Test (EMDA Math Reasoning) is a published norm-referenced instrument derived from WIAT-II, but it was selected by the partner district as curriculum-aligned, so treat as standardized/independent.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Wolf Trap arts-integrated mathematics PD vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Early Math Diagnostic Assessment (EMDA) Math Reasoning test (45 items; Pearson/PsychCorp, derived from WIAT-II)
effect_sizes.timepoint: spring Year 2 (end of treatment; two-year impact)
effect_sizes.g_method: g = J*d, with d=0.21 taken directly from report (footnote 10: raw mean difference 1.8 / pooled within-group posttest SD; J=0.998). g_var = [(n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c))]*J^2 using n_t/n_c estimated from analysis N=334 split in proportion to assessed Y2 T/C ratio 198:156. SD standardizing = pooled within-group EMDA SD (value not reported).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.16-17, Exhibit 10 (printed pp.16-17); Appendix B pp.B-2/B-3
effect_sizes.notes: Headline two-year (end-of-treatment) student-achievement impact; p<.01 per the report's HLM. This is the immediate post-intervention wave for the 2-year program. Reported ES 0.21 is the unadjusted student-level d; the HLM that produced the p-value adjusts for baseline EMDA and covariates and accounts for clustering, but neither its coefficient nor SE is reported. N=334 students, 18 schools for the Year-2 analysis.
